newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian presidency agrees on Papal invitation.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian presidency agrees on Papal invitation.

text.p: Bosnia's three-man presidency has agreed to support an invitation for a visit by Pope John Paul to Sarajevo, a German diplomat said on Saturday.

"The presidency has...supported an earlier invitation by President Izetbegovic for the Pope to come to Sarajevo. This has been endorsed by consensus," Ambassador Michael Steiner told reporters in Sarajevo.
Steiner, deputy to the international community's High Representative to Bosnia, spent Saturday meeting with Bosnia's tripartite presidency, which consists of a Moslem, a Croat and a Serb.

Pope John Paul had planned to visit Sarajevo during the height of the Bosnia war in 1994 but his trip was cancelled at the last minute because Serbs besieging the city refused to guarantee his safety.
The Pope has spoken often of Sarajevo in recent years and he is reported to view the city as a symbol of world suffering.
Alija Izetbegovic, a Moslem who led Bosnia's war-time government and is now president of the post-war presidency, was always keen on a Papal visit to reinforce the country's multi-ethnic identity.
Bosnia's Catholic Croats were always supportive of the Pope's coming and now the Orthodox Serb member of the three-man presidency has given his support as well.
